review.review_note: Approved by the operator for a proof-of-concept running on synthetic seed consultations. This is NOT independent clinical review. Every term is already present as a canonical in medical_lexicon.txt, but those records were also developer self-review and declare intended_consumer=live_post_asr_normalizer, so this inventory changes the consumer as well as the mechanism. Do not describe this list as clinically reviewed.

selection_method: Each target is a term spoken in a captured consultation that the corrected lane still renders incorrectly. Terms the corrected lane already handles are carried as controls so a regression is visible. No term was added from a drug reference; every one has a measured miss or a measured success behind it.

phrases.rationale: One character from correct in the corrected lane. The registered lexicon variant is `Luratidine`, which also does not match, so string replacement cannot reach it.
Corrected lane lands close but wrong. Observed misrendered in every captured note wording for this consult.

The corrected lane produces the registered lexicon variant `Pyritin`. Two candidate fixes exist - decode-time boosting, or lifting the ADR-011 lexicon bypass for a curated subset - so this term is the one that distinguishes the two mechanisms.
Correction already fixes this outright, both occurrences. Present so the arm proves boosting does not regress a term the lane already gets right.
Correct in both lanes across three deterministic replays. A regression here would indicate boosting is destabilising already-correct output.

phrases.live_lane_produced: NFL electric reaction / and aphylactic reaction
phrases.rationale: The highest-stakes recovery observed: correction rescued the diagnosis from an unrecognisable live rendering. Carried as a control because the lane already succeeds; a regression here would be the most serious possible outcome of this arm.

hard_negatives.must: never appear in a corrected transcript for these fixtures
hard_negatives.evidence: The summariser substituted this real OTC antihistamine unprompted in the 2026-07-21 note for consult-1.2, where it appears in no transcript lane. Boosting must not make the same substitution acoustically.

hard_negatives.must: never appear in a corrected transcript
hard_negatives.evidence: A prescription antiparasitic. Captured notes drifted toward this token from `pyritin`. Phonetic proximity to a boosted term is exactly the failure mode to guard.

hard_negatives.must: not be rewritten when used as an ordinary English word
hard_negatives.evidence: The live lane's rendering of Piriton. Boosting Piriton must not capture legitimate non-clinical uses.

hard_negatives.must: behave exactly as before when the inventory is inactive
hard_negatives.evidence: The historical single approved phrase. Retained so the pre-inventory behaviour stays provable.

not_in_scope: Any term not spoken in a captured consultation.
Proper nouns, patient or clinician names, addresses, and clinic identifiers.
Dosages, frequencies, and routes - boosting a number is not a recognition fix.
Terms whose only evidence is a note rendering; the note is downstream of the lane this inventory targets.
